title: Hurricane and tropical storm
summary: Watch means within 48 hours, warning within 36. Inland risks: wind, power loss, flash floods, tornadoes.

sources.title: 12 On Your Side: Hurricane Isabel, 20 years later

blocks.text: Henrico is inland, but hurricanes still reach it. Expect **wind-downed trees and power lines, flash flooding, tornadoes spun off by the storm,** and flooding on the James River. Hurricane Isabel in September 2003 left more than 2 million people without power.

rows: A storm is possible within **48 hours**
A storm is expected within **36 hours**

blocks.text: Atlantic season runs **June 1 to November 30**, peaking mid-August to late October.

items: Learn about evacuation. Virginia's Know Your Zone program covers coastal localities. It does **not** cover Henrico, so follow Henrico officials.
Use several alert sources: Emergency Alert System, Wireless Emergency Alerts (no sign-up), the FEMA app, NOAA Weather Radio.
Charge your phone and get backup chargers when a hurricane is forecast. Stock medicine, disinfectant, pet supplies.
Keep copies of insurance policies and IDs in a password-protected digital space.
Clear gutters and drains. Bring in outdoor furniture.
**Flood insurance takes effect 30 days after you buy it**, and homeowner or renter insurance doesn't cover flood loss.
Keep help in mind: government help can take several days or weeks to arrive. Pet kits: at least 3 days of food, water and medicine.
Watch alerts. If officials order evacuation for your area, **leave immediately**.
In high wind, go to an interior room or a storm shelter.
If flooding traps you, go to the highest level. **Don't go into a closed attic.**
**Never walk, swim or drive through flood water.** 6 inches of moving water can knock you down. 1 foot can sweep a car away.
Generators go outside, at least 20 feet from the house.
**Stay out of flood water.** It can hide debris and electrified lines.
Don't touch wet electrical equipment or anything while standing in water. If safe, turn off power at the main breaker.
Stay away from downed power lines. Report them to Dominion at 866-366-4357.
Wear protective clothing and a mask when cleaning mold or debris. Work with a partner. Children should not help.
**Save phone calls for emergencies.** Text instead.
Take photos of damage for insurance.
